relations.definition: Assigns an inference step a declared position in this argument reconstruction. Position is local to the claim context; partial and competing reconstructions remain possible. Neither sequence, logical validity nor chronological occurrence is inferred.

inverse_labels.default: is used as a premise in
inverse_labels.en: is used as a premise in

relations.definition: Assigns a thesis the premise role in this particular inference step. The same thesis may have another role elsewhere, or be granted hypothetically without endorsement. Its truth is not entailed.

Assigns a thesis the conclusion role in this step. This records the reconstructed reasoning, not proof that the conclusion follows or is true. Multiple conclusions or rival reconstructions need not be collapsed.

An interpretation that this thesis belongs to the situated conception within the declared scope. Membership is neither truth, exhaustive coverage nor universal commitment of everyone associated with the conception.

inverse_labels.default: has an argument offered in support
inverse_labels.en: has an argument offered in support

relations.definition: Identifies what an argument is offered to support, not whether it succeeds. The relation is distinct from a conclusion's local role in an inference step.
Targets the specific inferential transition, not automatically the truth of its premises or rejection of the whole argument. The challenge account and relation basis state the contested feature.
Targets this proposition or its conditions as explicitly explained in the relation basis. A challenge is not a proof of negation; a premise may be challenged separately from the transition using it.
Targets the identified reasoning structure as a whole under the declared scope. Use objection_to_step for a specific transition; this relation does not silently manufacture targets for every part.
Targets specified commitments of a situated conception, not a shared concept, the existence of its thinker or all associated theses.
Relates a substantive challenge to reasoning offered to develop it. The two referents remain distinct; neither mutual support nor a cycle in discussion proves circular reasoning or validity.

An evidence-bearing interpretation linking a specified thought object to an intellectual or textual object. This is not an exact occurrence anchor, authorship, literal quotation, complete coverage or endorsement.

A scoped attribution of a thought object to an individual or collective, distinct from the maker of this research Claim. A premise granted for reductio is not automatically endorsed, and attribution need not be exclusive.

A grounded membership assertion explaining which continuity criterion and shared problem connects this particular conception to this crosscutting concept. Shared spelling, translation or topic labels alone do not suffice. Multiple competing memberships and explicit denials may coexist; membership asserts neither identical definitions nor canonical acceptance.

labels.default: is attributed as a conception to
labels.en: is attributed as a conception to

relations.definition: An attribution of this situated account to a responsibility bearer or collective, within the Claim's declared scope. The maker of the attribution is separate from the attributed thinker; attribution does not establish endorsement of every quoted statement or exclusive authorship.

inverse_labels.default: is interpreted as expressing a conception
inverse_labels.en: is interpreted as expressing a conception

relations.definition: An evidence-bearing interpretation that a specified intellectual or textual object expresses this conception. Expression is not authorship, complete coverage, acceptance, identical wording, or an unqualified statement by the object creator.

The subject conception gives a materially changed definition of the object conception's problem or commitments. The Claim explains retained and changed features; similarity, chronology, record correction, translation and direct influence are not entailed.

The subject conception rejects specified commitments of the object conception. The Claim identifies the rejected content and its scope; polemic is not total contradiction, psychological hostility, or rejection of the shared concept.

The subject conception restricts the object conception's declared scope or application. The Claim identifies the comparison dimension and boundary; graph subset, later chronology and a shorter description do not establish this relation.

The subject conception extends the object conception's declared scope or application. The Claim identifies the comparison dimension and added scope; additional text or graph neighbors alone do not establish expansion.

The subject conception reworks specified religious or theological commitments of the object conception in a declared non-theological register. The Claim states which commitments and comparison justify the description; neither progress nor total removal of religious meaning is entailed.

The subject conception reworks specified features of the object conception in terms of mental processes or psychological explanation. The Claim names those features and grounds; this relation neither diagnoses a person nor establishes causal influence.

The subject conception reworks specified features of the object conception in a political scope of power, institutions or collective action. The Claim states its comparison and grounds; mere political context is insufficient.

The subject conception reverses a specified ordering, valuation, opposition or explanatory direction of the object conception. The Claim names what is reversed; visual direction, logical negation, reciprocal relations or record version order alone do not establish inversion.

A source claim about who sends or purports to send a letter. Sender is not automatically author, copyist, printer or the person who physically carries it; an addressed draft need not have been dispatched.
A source claim identifying the intended addressee of correspondence. Addressing does not establish delivery, actual reading, agreement, intellectual influence or authorship.

An evidence-bound attribution of a document to a persistent physical artifact. It does not equate the intellectual document with its carrier or guarantee autograph status, complete preservation, textual equivalence, custody or reuse rights. Different copies may be different carriers.

A claim linking a historical situation with a document relevant to its reconstruction. The evidence must explain the association; mere proximity, a shared date or a title does not establish participation, chronology, causation or source independence.

inverse_labels.default: is identified as subject of document
inverse_labels.en: is identified as subject of document

relations.definition: A source-attributed claim that a document concerns a Work, including scholarly identification when the document does not name the work explicitly. It is not necessarily a verbatim mention, quotation, authorship attribution or historical influence.

inverse_labels.default: is time anchor for dating claim
inverse_labels.en: is time anchor for dating claim

relations.definition: A relative dating Claim explicitly names this historical situation as its temporal anchor. The original before, after, during or overlaps qualifier remains in the date value. The edge alone asserts no chronology and implies no absolute date or causal influence.

An evidence-bound dating of a historical situation, distinct from witness creation, data capture and knowledge revision. Exact, approximate, disputed, unknown and relative dates do not imply one another. Competing datings remain separate Claims; numerical comparison never accepts the assertion.

A claim assigning an Agent or Organization to a historical situation with an explicit contextual participation role. Presence, authorship, responsibility and causal influence are not implied by one another.
A claim relating a historical situation to a normalized Place in its stated spatial and temporal scope. It does not assert political belonging, permanent residence or causal influence.
A source-owned topical association of a historical situation with a Work. Creation, publication, reading, reception and influence remain more specific claims; this relation implies none of them.

Stand-off asserted_by link explicitly present in the source packet. It records structure, not acceptance of the associated interpretation.
Root of the semantic interchange relation hierarchy; it does not erase source-native predicates.
Explicit fallback for a source-native predicate that has no reviewed semantic interchange mapping yet.
Stable interchange family for source-native conceptual predicates; predicate_id preserves the exact authored relation such as develops_concept or influences.

source_mappings.definition: Source-declared genre classification; neither identity nor authorship.
Source-declared development of the target concept; the source review posture remains authoritative.
A directional influence claim, not equivalence, necessary causation, or an automatically transitive relation.
Source-declared polemical engagement; it neither establishes influence nor requires reciprocal engagement.
Source-declared conceptual transformation; the target is not thereby identical to the source.

relations.definition: Stable interchange family for historical placement while retaining the exact source-native predicate_id.
Stable interchange family for transmission, commentary, translation, preservation and survival predicates without collapsing their source-native identity.
Stable interchange family for contestation and explicitly uncertain source relations; it never upgrades them to accepted truth.
Stable interchange family for declared language and script use; exact predicate_id distinguishes language from script.
Derived workbench relation that counts requested node or relation vocabulary; it is not a philosophical assertion.
Derived atlas and workbench containment or preparation route; it carries navigation, not philosophical truth.

labels.default: links to an access or description surface
labels.ru: связывает с поверхностью доступа или описания
labels.en: links to an access or description surface

relations.definition: Connects a source object to a declared Link identity; predicate_id retains whether the link describes, supplies metadata, states rights, or permits download.
Stable interchange family for the bounded relation vocabulary embedded directly in authored ToS node contracts; predicate_id preserves the exact subtype.
Stable interchange family for predicates owned by the ToS canon predicate registry; predicate_id preserves the exact registered subtype and its source authority.
Root for source-tree and repository topology relations that do not assert philosophical meaning.
Contains another navigation or repository projection object; it is not geographic containment.
Connects a repository branch projection to its indexed manifest representation.
Connects a repository branch projection to an indexed resource representation.
Connects a philosophy branch route to an authored source-planting record.
Connects one source planting to its declared witness backlog anchor without asserting canon.
Connects two carrier representations that declare the same persistent ToS entity identity; it is not a new same-as judgment.
Inverse vocabulary entry for tos.relation.projects; stored graph edges remain in the projects direction.
Root for evidence-bearing Work, Expression, Edition, Collection, Item and File topology predicates.
Relates a Work to an Expression through an evidence-bearing claim.
Relates an Expression to an Edition without implying textual equivalence.
Relates an Edition to one acquired Item through an evidence-bearing claim.
Connects one Item to an immutable content-addressed File from its manifest.
Relates a Collection to a member Work through an evidence-bearing membership claim.
A directed non-transitive Expression derivation claim that does not establish equivalence.
Root for role-specific responsibility claims; roles are relations, not Agent subclasses.

Relates a Work or Document to the Agent carrying the author role through a claim. Authorship is distinct from sending, addressing, copying or owning its carrier; competing attributions remain separate Claims.
Relates an Expression to the Agent carrying the translator role through a claim.
Relates an intellectual object to the Agent carrying an editor role through a claim.
Relates an intellectual object to the Agent responsible for an afterword.
Relates an intellectual object to a role-bearing contributor when a narrower responsibility predicate is unavailable.
Relates an intellectual object to the Agent carrying a design responsibility role.
Root for reified claim, evidence, maker, provenance and review edges.
Connects a reified Claim to its subject representation.
Connects a reified Claim to its identity or literal object representation.
Connects a reified Claim to one source-returnable Evidence object.
Connects a reified Claim to its recorded maker representation.
Connects a reified Claim to the provenance event that generated its recorded form.
Connects a claim to a normalized Place while preserving literal form and spatial role separately.
Connects a claim to a normalized Agent or Organization while preserving the role separately.
Relates a Work to a claim-scoped chronology with explicit interval, stages, precision and ordering warning.
Relates an Edition to a claim-scoped provision activity with typed roles, places and temporal assertion.
Generic claim predicate for a named temporal facet that is not first-publication chronology.
Root for explicit semantic handoffs between source, claim, canon and projection layers.
States that one explicit representation stands for another identified object under a source-owned assertion.
Connects a semantic object or claim to the exact source identity or evidence that grounds it.
A source-owned topical relation that must not be inferred from labels or text similarity alone.
A reviewed identity-equivalence assertion; shared labels, paths or similar text never create it automatically.
